title: On-call & Incident Response: Standards, Runbooks, and Templates
author: Jordan Patel
body:
Summary:
This document centralizes Redwood Inference’s on-call and incident response standards, runbook expectations, postmortem workflow, on-call rotation rules, game day guidance, and customer-facing status page / comms templates. It is intended to be a single reference for SREs, on-call engineers, incident commanders, and engineering managers.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Ensure reliable, consistent, and auditable response to production incidents that affect uptime, latency, data integrity, or customer experience.
- Scope: All production services owned by Redwood Inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Includes infra and application-layer incidents, security incidents (see security-and-compliance for sensitive workflows), and external dependency outages.

Incident severity definitions (use these to classify incidents on initial triage):
1) Sev 1 (P0) - Major outage: service unavailable or critical customer workflows broken for >5% of tenants or any customer facing SLA breach. Immediate pager, incident declared.
2) Sev 2 (P1) - Degraded critical functionality: increased error rate or latency that materially impacts customers but partial operation continues. Pager and on-call action.
3) Sev 3 (P2) - Non-critical degradation: feature regressions or degraded background processing with limited customer impact. Email/Slack notification and scheduled follow-up.
4) Sev 4 (P3) - Informational / maintenance: planned maintenance, non-customer-facing updates. Document change window.

On-call roster & rotations:
- Primary on-call (service owner): 1-week rotation, Monday 09:00 -> next Monday 09:00 local office time.
- Secondary on-call (backup for escalation): 2-week rotation, overlap for handover and shadowing.
- Paging sequence: primary -> secondary -> EngSRE lead -> engineering manager on-call.
- Handover: Each shift must post a handover note in #oncall-handoffs Slack channel with key incidents, ongoing mitigations, and outstanding actions.
- Time off: If unavailable, update PagerDuty schedule and notify the rotation lead two business days prior.

Alerting & escalation policy:
- Alerts must have runbook link and playbook summary in the PagerDuty alert body.
- If an alert is unacknowledged for 2 minutes, escalate to the next responder. If no acknowledgement in 10 minutes for Sev1, incident commander is auto-notified.
- All Sev1 incidents require an Incident Commander (IC) and a Communications Lead within 10 minutes of declaration.

Incident response runbook (high-level procedure):
1) Detect and Triage (0-10 minutes):
   - Acknowledge the pager. Record alert ID and time.
   - Determine scope and impact (services, customers, regions). Capture initial severity.
   - Check dashboards: latency, error rates, traffic distribution, infra metrics.
2) Declare (10-20 minutes if Sev1):
   - IC declares incident in #incidents Slack channel and creates an incident room (Slack channel or bridge).
   - Create incident document in the incident tracker template and assign roles: Incident Commander, Scribe, Communications Lead, Recovery Leads.
3) Mitigate (20-90 minutes):
   - Run targeted mitigations from service runbook (examples below). Prefer reversible actions.
   - If rolling back, use documented rollback playbooks and follow change freeze rules.
4) Communicate (ongoing):
   - Post an initial public status (see templates below) within 30 minutes for Sev1 impacting customers.
   - Update status every 30-60 minutes or when there is a material change.
5) Recovery & Root Cause (after service restored):
   - Maintain incident channel for coordination until stable for 2 hours.
   - Begin evidence collection and timeline for postmortem.
6) Postmortem (within 72 hours):
   - Draft postmortem in the postmortem template. Assign author (usually IC or Scribe).
   - Include timeline, impact, RCA, contributing factors, corrective actions (owner + SLA for completion).

Runbook best practices (per-service):
- Each service must have a one-page runbook and a detailed playbook. The one-page runbook must include: owner, PagerDuty escalation policy, quick triage checks, safe mitigations, rollback steps, and safe commands.
- Minimum fields for runbook table (example):

Service | Owner | Runbook link | Key commands / checks
-------|-------|--------------|-------------------
api-gateway | @alice | /runbooks/api-gateway | `kubectl logs -l app=api-gateway`
router | @bob | /runbooks/router | `redis-cli INFO`
inference-runtime | @charlie | /runbooks/inference-runtime | `nvtop`, `tail -f /var/log/runtime.log`

- If runbook requires secrets or elevated access, reference the secure runbook and list contact for elevated ops.

Postmortem process and template (minimum):
- Timeline: Start drafting within 24 hours; circulate to reviewers within 72 hours; publish final postmortem within 7 days.
- Required sections: Summary, Impact (customers affected and duration), Timeline of events, Root Cause Analysis, Mitigations taken, Action items (owner + due date), Follow-up / monitoring changes, Lessons learned.
- Postmortem review: 1-hour blameless review with stakeholders within 7 days. Decision on whether changes require RFC/ADR.

Action item tracking:
- All action items must be tracked in the engineering backlog with clear owner and target completion date. Label with `incident-<INCIDENT_ID>` and include link in postmortem.

Game days (exercises):
- Frequency: Quarterly team-level game days; annual company-wide disaster recovery exercise.
- Goals: Validate runbooks, alerting, status page workflows, and cross-team communications.
- Format: Simulated incident declared, conduct full response, verify status page updates, runbook effectiveness, and post-incident debrief.
- Success criteria: Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) < 2 minutes, Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) within service SLO targets, clear postmortem produced within 7 days.

Status page and customer communication templates (use placeholders):
- Minimal public status page messages for customer-facing incidents. Keep language factual and avoid technical speculation.

Initial public status (template):
Title: "[Service] Degraded - Investigation Underway"
Body:
We are currently investigating reports of degraded performance for [SERVICE]. Some customers may experience increased latency or errors.
Impact: [brief description, e.g. "API requests failing for 10% of customers in us-west-2"].
Timestamp: [2026-01-10T14:12:00Z]
What we are doing: Our on-call team is actively investigating and working on mitigation. We will provide updates every 30 minutes or as the situation changes.

Customer update (template):
Title: "Update: [Service] - Mitigation in progress"
Body:
Status: Mitigation in progress. We have identified [component] as correlated with the issue and have deployed a mitigation to reduce impact. Some customers may still experience intermittent errors.
Next update: [time or condition]

Resolution notice (template):
Title: "Resolved: [Service]"
Body:
We have restored full service for [SERVICE] as of [timestamp]. Root cause analysis is ongoing and a postmortem will be published within 7 days. If you continue to see issues, please contact support@redwood-inference.com and reference incident [INCIDENT_ID].

Internal communication checklist (IC & Comms Lead):
- Announce incident in #incidents Slack channel and create room.
- Assign Roles: IC, Scribe, Comms, Recovery Leads.
- Post initial public status if customer impact.
- Keep legal/security informed for incidents affecting customer data.

Incident documentation & auditability:
- Every incident must have a single canonical incident doc (use the incident-template page) with timestamps in UTC, a list of commands run, logs, and links to dashboards and runbooks.
- Attach relevant traces, screenshots, and support tickets.

Metrics & SLOs to track during an incident:
- Pager volume (alerts/min by service)
- MTTA (mean time to acknowledge) - target < 2m for Sev1
- MTTM (mean time to mitigate) - service-specific targets
- Number of customer-facing errors and percentage of affected customers

Appendix: Common quick mitigations (examples)
- API 500 errors: Check recent deploys -> `kubectl rollout status` -> rollback if unhealthy.
- High GPU memory usage: Restart worker pool with drained connections; rotate to healthy nodes.
- Redis errors: Check persistence and run `redis-cli INFO` -> increase maxclients or failover according to runbook.

Contacts and ownership:

This document is intended to be updated iteratively. If you find gaps in runbooks, add a TODO with owner and open a small RFC if the change affects cross-team behavior.
